best_field_traits: Warm-season signalgrass with several short, often erect or ascending, densely spikeleted flowering branches.
Plump blunt obovoid mature spikelets around 2.4–3 mm, one basal reduced/sterile floret and a fertile upper floret.
Lower glume relatively short: Kew/AusGrass commonly ~1/4–1/3 spikelet, but UT's 1–1.3 mm on 2.9–3.4 mm spikelets sometimes exceeds 1/3. Measure actual ripe glumes; do not apply a hard ratio cutoff.
Upper glume and sterile lower lemma with visible crossveins under magnification; upper fertile lemma tough and transversely wrinkled.
Soft broad grass blade, as seen in original source photo, but leaf width alone not diagnostic.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Full tuft and base (annual/perennial status confirmation)
Full dense flowering head with scale
One 2.4–3 mm ripe spikelet face and edge
Lower glume relative to entire spikelet length
True ligule and collar, visible sheath
crew_field_check: FIRST PHOTO: follow the original clustered greenish flowering head; the yellowish spikelets along short side racemes are visible, not individually measured.
MEASURE 5–10 ripe intact spikelets beside a 1-mm ruler; U. fusca commonly ~2.4–3.4 mm in Kew/UT descriptions.
At 10–20×, turn an entire spikelet sideways: lower glume ~1/4–1/3 length, upper glume extends near apex, sometimes conspicuous cross-veins.
The separate James Schnable greenhouse photograph teaches vegetative blade posture ONLY, not wild range, glume anatomy or an exposed ligule.
Distinguish from tiny U. reptans and large U. texana by the combined measured spikelet size, lower glume and paired floret structure; if missing, label Urochloa sp.

comparisons.key_distinctions: A photographed mature spikelet is the test: U. reptans usually 1.5–2.2 mm with lower glume only about 1/8–1/4 of its length, while U. texana is substantially larger (4.5–5.9 mm) and its lower glume normally reaches about half to two-thirds. U. fusca can be rather open or dense depending stage; do not treat head compactness as a yes/no species test.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Measure 5–10 ripe spikelets from each vouchered plant at the same scale, then expose the lower glume on one intact spikelet.
field_matrix.separating_characters: Brownseed U. fusca has plumper 2.4–3.4 mm spikelets; creeping U. reptans usually has smaller 1.5–2.2 mm spikelets. Reptans lower glume is only about 1/8–1/4 of the spikelet (UT approximately 0.5 mm); fusca has a longer lower glume (UT approximately 1–1.3 mm on 2.9–3.4 mm spikelets). Both can have rooting lower nodes; do not decide from a prostrate stem.
field_matrix.caution: The 1/4–1/3 fusca ratio is a broad-description approximation: UT's 1–1.3 mm glume on a 2.9–3.4 mm spikelet can exceed 1/3. Use actual mature measurements and the whole suite of characters, not a rigid ratio cutoff.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Measure ripe spikelets and both glumes side by side, then open the true inner leaf collar at 10–20×.
field_matrix.separating_characters: U. fusca has 2.4–3.4 mm spikelets and a relatively short lower glume (UT about 1–1.3 mm); U. texana has conspicuously larger 4.5–5.9 mm spikelets with a 2.4–3.2 mm lower glume, about half to two-thirds the spikelet. Fusca's ligule is a short hair fringe; texana has a ciliate membranous ligule about 1–1.8 mm. Neither has a conspicuous long fertile-lemma awn.
field_matrix.caution: A whole flowering-head photo cannot establish glume lengths, venation, ligule type, or a millimeter measurement; the present target photographs do not resolve those characters.

not_reliable_alone: Inferring lower-glume length or cross-veins from original distant head photo
Calling every tight yellow-headed Urochloa U. fusca; ripeness and branch angle vary
Calling wild county nativity from a greenhouse plant

field_id_finish_pass.crew_teaching_summary: BROWNSEED SIGNALGRASS: start with a tallish branching head of multiple usually ascending spikelet-bearing racemes, then look for plump blunt obovoid spikelets (roughly 2.4–3.4 mm depending source). Lower glume is relatively short, commonly about ONE-QUARTER to ONE-THIRD of the whole spikelet. The existing flowering photograph supports the clustered head, not the glume proportions; confirm on ripe material with a millimeter scale.
field_id_finish_pass.lookalike_comparison: A photographed mature spikelet is the test: U. reptans usually 1.5–2.2 mm with lower glume only about 1/8–1/4 of its length, while U. texana is substantially larger (4.5–5.9 mm) and its lower glume normally reaches about half to two-thirds. U. fusca can be rather open or dense depending stage; do not treat head compactness as a yes/no species test.
photo_targets: Ripe 2.4–3.4 mm spikelet face and edge with a 1-mm ruler, correctly vouchered
Lower glume base and length with both glumes attached (10–20×)
Same plant whole raceme arrangement and basal nodes
True ligule and hairy sheath/collar macro; leaf posture photograph already supplied by Commons
field_id_finish_pass.photo_limit: The original source picture resolves flowering racemes/leaf surfaces but not the microscopic lower glume, veins, ciliate ligule or true mm spikelet measurements. Commons supplementary panels are separately credited.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.look_here_first: BROWNSEED SIGNALGRASS: follow 3–20 short one-sided racemes on the terminal axis, then turn ONE mature plump 2.4–3.0 mm spikelet sideways. Its tiny LOWER glume occupies about 1/4–1/3 of spikelet length; do not guess this from the current head photo. Verify the true 1-mm HAIR-FRINGE ligule and an ANNUAL base before species certification.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.measured_growth_and_collar: Annual, decumbent or branching culms approximately 30–120 cm; lower nodes can root, but true rhizomes and stolons are absent in AusGrass. Nodes often hairy. Sheaths glabrous to tubercle-hispid, blades typically 5–15 mm wide. True ligule a fringe of hairs about 1 mm at blade–sheath junction (not a broad membrane). An annual with rooting low nodes is not automatically a perennial stoloniferous species.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.measured_panicle_and_spikelets: Central inflorescence axis about 6–15 cm; 3–20 unilateral racemes, each approximately 1–8 cm, with paired pedicelled, dorsally compressed obovoid spikelets approximately 2.4–3.0 mm. One lower male/sterile floret and one upper fertile floret; spikelet falls entire. Source descriptions and maturity may broaden observed spikelet length to roughly 3.4 mm; do not apply a single photo-derived threshold.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.measured_glumes_lemmas_and_awns: Lower glume membranous, clasping, ~1/4–1/3 of 2.4–3.0 mm spikelet (approximately 0.6–1.0 mm by proportional estimate, NOT an independently published absolute range), commonly 5-veined in Kew GrassBase; upper glume near full spikelet length, 7-veined, cross-veined. Lower sterile/male lemma ~full spikelet length, 7-veined and cross-veined, with palea. Upper fertile lemma hard, transversely rugose, approximately 2.2–2.8 mm, obtuse with inrolled margins; upper palea also firm. NO conspicuous long glume or fertile-lemma awn; do not mistake minute mucro or cross-veins for an awn.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.central_texas_lookalikes: Urochloa reptans: generally smaller 1.5–2.2 mm spikelets, lower glume only ~1/8–1/4, decumbent/rooting lower nodes. Urochloa texana: larger 4.5–5.9 mm mature spikelets, lower glume commonly ~1/2–2/3, ciliate membranous ligule (rather than fusca's simple hair fringe). Digitaria ciliaris: fingerlike flattened racemes and differently arranged paired spikelets; confirm its own glumes and floret surfaces. Head density and habitat alone cannot decide.
crew_id_sequence: LOOK HERE FIRST: inspect whole mature head, count one-sided racemes, and trace the same plant to a rooted annual base.
Open the actual leaf collar: photograph and measure ~1-mm HAIR-FRINGE ligule, distinguish from longer sheath and node hairs.
Measure 5–10 intact ripe spikelets at 10–20× with a 1-mm ruler; note length, pair attachment and branch position.
Rotate and open one spikelet: separately identify tiny lower glume, full-length upper glume, cross-veined lower sterile lemma and hard wrinkled upper fertile lemma.
Compare matched ripe U. reptans and U. texana at identical magnification; if anatomy is unresolved, label Urochloa sp., not a certified species.
diagnostic_photo_gaps: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: same-plant legally documented annual rooted crown and actual lower root-bearing node, with centimeter scale; do not use the greenhouse vegetative reference to claim a wild Hays occurrence.
NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: blade–sheath junction face-on at 10–20× with 1-mm ruler, showing true ~1-mm hair-fringe ligule separately from sheath hairs.
NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: 5–10 ripe 2.4–3.0(-3.4) mm attached spikelets with mm ruler; show paired pedicels and 1/4–1/3 lower-glume ratio.
NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: dissected upper/lower glumes, cross-veined lower lemma and rugose upper fertile lemma under 10–20×, with exact taxon provenance and license.
NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: matched measured ripe U. reptans and U. texana spikelets, not redundant distant head shots.

NEEDS_SITE_QA: physically verify all existing local JPEG bytes, per-image CC BY-NC/CC BY-SA conditions, author/source credit, visible gross-arrow endpoints and actual public learner rendering before upgrading status.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.public_ready_criteria: Keep FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS until licensed exact-species attached spikelet, true ligule and mature glume/lemma evidence are physically archived and independently inspected; arrows only on visible pixels. Confirm public rights and page render separately. No current photograph proves the 5/7 glume veins or actual 1-mm ligule.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Brownseed signalgrass: actual flowering habit → true ligule → attached spikelets
steps: BEGIN WITH THE LOCAL TEXAS FIELD PHOTO: Jim Conrad's actual Uvalde flower-bearing plant has long leaves and a branched head with relatively short flower-bearing arms. The roots aren't shown.

LOOK INSIDE THE LEAF COLLAR: Jim Conrad's Uvalde close-up clearly shows a dense WHITE HAIR-FRINGED ligule across the INNER junction of blade and sheath. This is not just hairs along the outside sheath.

LOOK AT AN ATTACHED REPRODUCTIVE BRANCH: the real Uvalde macro shows ovoid, green ribbed spikelets facing mainly ONE SIDE of their slender rachis, with conspicuous hairs. Keep labels on visible parts only.

NEXT REQUIRED PHOTO: place five or more fully mature spikelets by a real mm ruler; study the lower glume (roughly 1/4–1/3 the whole spikelet) and dissect a mature fertile lemma instead of estimating from a full head.
MATCH DIFFERENT-SPECIES LOOK-ALIKES: compare separately labelled U. reptans public-license photograph and actual U. texana close-up; do not mislabel their reproductive structures as U. fusca.
VIEW THE GREENHOUSE FOLIAGE PHOTO AS CONTEXT ONLY: long arching blades alone don't prove a species ID, rooted annual/perennial growth or its flowering anatomy.
PUBLIC PHOTO RIGHTS: the old Minnette Marr CC BY-NC photo is preserved in the archive with its creator information, but is intentionally excluded from the unrestricted public Learner.

OPTIONAL ADVANCED REFERENCE: two 2019 Yucatán Jim Conrad photos show true ruler comparisons and early roots on a creeping node, but the photographer himself was uncertain they were U. fusca. They are marked Urochloa cf. fusca and do not certify a diagnostic role.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: In the actual Uvalde plant, pair the visible inner white hair-fringe LIGULE with one-sided ovoid attached spikelets; then confirm a mature measured glume/lemma before final species diagnosis. A photo of another Urochloa species is only a comparison.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Actual ligule and attached spikelet images exist and are hosted locally; no physical 1-mm ruler on 2014 Uvalde macro. One NC archived image held from public display; only public-licensed comparisons retained. No full mature measured glume dissection, species-authenticated exposed adventitious roots or mobile Pages QA yet.

what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Ripe 2.4–3.4 mm spikelet face and edge with a 1-mm ruler, correctly vouchered
Lower glume base and length with both glumes attached (10–20×)
Same plant whole raceme arrangement and basal nodes
True ligule and hairy sheath/collar macro; leaf posture photograph already supplied by Commons

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — THE HEAD
field_id_short_tiles.short: Count 3–20 one-sided flowering racemes on ONE intact stem.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Existing target photo panel 1 (index 0) genuinely shows the clustered flowering head. Count the lateral racemes and trace their attachment; neither glume veins nor ripe spikelet lengths are resolved in this picture. A compact head alone is not a species identification.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · BASE AND TRUE COLLAR
field_id_short_tiles.short: Annual base; true ligule is a ~1 mm FRINGE OF HAIRS.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Follow the same plant down to its annual crown; low nodes may root, but the current definitive U. fusca gallery does not expose a connected rooted flowering base. Open species panel 2 (index 1): Jim Conrad's Uvalde photograph ACTUALLY shows the white hair-fringe true ligule across the inner blade–sheath junction. It lacks a physical 1-mm scale, so a calibrated ligule measurement remains a photo gap. Panel 5 (index 4) instead shows tentative Yucatán Urochloa cf. fusca spikelets, NOT a ligule or authenticated rooted U. fusca.
field_id_short_tiles.status: TRUE INNER LIGULE PHOTOGRAPH VERIFIED — SCALE AND ROOTED BASE STILL NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · MEASURE RIPE SPIKELETS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Usually 2.4–3.0 mm; published variation reaches ~3.4 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Open source-identified Uvalde U. fusca panel 3 (index 2): it REALLY shows intact ribbed, ovoid spikelets on one side of a rachis, but without a ruler or exposed individual glumes. Measure 5–10 ripe attached spikelets at 10–20× with a real millimeter scale; published dimensions are generally ~2.4–3.4 mm, not dimensions certified by panel 3. Panel 5 (index 4) has a ruler but is Yucatán Urochloa cf. fusca with tentative taxon identity; NEVER count its measurements as verified U. fusca anatomy.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL ATTACHED SPIKELETS VERIFIED — CALIBRATED EXACT-SPECIES DISSECTION MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · SEPARATE THE BRACTS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower glume short but NOT a fixed ≤1/3 rule; upper glume near full length.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Lower glume short relative to spikelet; UT measures ~1–1.3 mm on 2.9–3.4 mm spikelets, so a strict 1/3 cutoff is unsafe. Upper glume near full length. At 10–20× separate both glumes, the cross-veined lower sterile/male lemma and hard transversely wrinkled upper fertile lemma (~2.2–2.9 mm across Kew/AusGrass). Kew reports commonly 5 veins on lower and 7 on upper glume; UT notes lower-glume vein variation. The fertile lemma lacks a conspicuous long awn; a tiny mucro is not one. All measurements are source-based, not current-photo measurements.
field_id_short_tiles.status: DIAGNOSTIC DISSECTION MISSING — NO MICRO ARROWS

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · LOCAL LOOK-ALIKES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Compare RIPE spikelet length and lower-glume proportion.
field_id_short_tiles.details: REAL DIFFERENT-SPECIES comparisons: panel 7 (index 6) is U. reptans; panels 8–9 (indices 7–8) are U. texana. Do not treat U. fusca's true ligule panel 2 (index 1), attached spikelets panel 3 (index 2), or greenhouse foliage panel 4 (index 3) as look-alikes. Published ripe-spikelet ranges: U. reptans ~1.5–2.2 mm with lower glume ~1/8–1/4; U. fusca ~2.4–3.4 mm with lower glume often ~1/4–1/3 (UT measured glumes may exceed 1/3); U. texana ~4.5–5.9 mm with lower glume ~1/2–2/3. Use actual same-scale measured glumes; if unresolved, label Urochloa sp.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL LOOK-ALIKE PHOTOS — SCALE NOT MATCHED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE
field_id_short_tiles.details: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: one source-verified same-plant U. fusca rooted annual base and lower node; an additional 1-mm calibrated inner hair-fringe ligule (the unscaled TRUE ligule already exists); 5–10 calibrated mature attached spikelets and dissected lower/upper glumes, lower sterile/male lemma, and hard fertile lemma; matched mature U. reptans/U. texana measurements. NEEDS_SITE_QA: check 7 real JPEGs, 10 teaching panels, 19 preserved existing gross markers, correct 4 definitive/2 tentative/1 NC-held evidence labels, per-photo rights and credits, public filtering, and mobile learner rendering. Do not call the species anatomically FINISHED.
field_id_short_tiles.status: HANDOFF TO PHOTO AND SITE-QA LANES
